timestamp_semantics.meaning: Timestamp reported by the upstream provider for the observation/version.
timestamp_semantics.selection_rule: Requires source semantics and provenance; not automatically trusted as first public availability.
timestamp_semantics.notes: Keep original value and normalized UTC value.

timestamp_semantics.meaning: When this project captured/retrieved the evidence.
timestamp_semantics.selection_rule: Conservative upper bound on knowability and fallback when earlier public availability cannot be defended.
timestamp_semantics.notes: Distinct retrievals remain distinct even for identical bytes.

timestamp_semantics.meaning: Earliest defensible time the exact information/version was publicly knowable.
timestamp_semantics.selection_rule: Must be <= forecast/training feature cutoff for eligibility.
timestamp_semantics.notes: Derived from evidence policy; never guessed from season labels.

timestamp_semantics.meaning: Start of the real-world interval/state for which the observation applies.
timestamp_semantics.selection_rule: Target/event time must lie in interval when the domain is interval-valued.
timestamp_semantics.notes: Future-effective facts may be known before valid_from.

timestamp_semantics.meaning: Exclusive end of the real-world interval/state for which the observation applies.
timestamp_semantics.selection_rule: Target/event time must be < valid_to when present.

timestamp_semantics.meaning: Point effective time for a rule/state/change when interval semantics begin at one instant.
timestamp_semantics.selection_rule: Applied to target/event time, not substituted for knowledge time.
timestamp_semantics.notes: Usually equivalent to valid_from for point changes.

timestamp_semantics.meaning: Earliest defensible knowledge time under a named PIT policy version.
timestamp_semantics.selection_rule: Cache/derived field only; query still checks target validity, domain policy, revision state and cutoff.
timestamp_semantics.notes: Not a raw source timestamp and never sufficient alone.

rules.title: No feature-source bypass
rules.rule: All feature construction must request observations through the PIT gateway/as-of interface.

rules.title: Knowledge cutoff
rules.rule: Observation first_known_at/policy-derived knowledge time must not exceed feature cutoff.

rules.title: Target validity
rules.rule: Observation must be valid/applicable for the target event/state time where the domain requires validity intervals.

rules.title: Revision replay
rules.rule: A revision/correction first known after the cutoff cannot replace the version that was knowable at the cutoff.

rules.title: Unknown timing fails closed
rules.rule: Missing/ambiguous temporal evidence cannot be guessed into PIT eligibility.

rules.title: Retrospective evidence
rules.rule: Retrospective/current pages require dated corroboration before historical use.

rules.title: Historical game completion
rules.rule: Same-game/future-game outcomes cannot enter pregame features; prior-game outputs require completion before cutoff.

rules.title: Market lane isolation
rules.rule: Market evidence is excluded from pure-football lane and is timestamp-gated in market-augmented lane.

rules.title: Weather run lineage
rules.rule: Issued weather feature requires exact model/run availability and target-valid time; observed truth cannot replace earlier forecast.

rules.title: Availability noncoverage
rules.rule: No official report outside policy scope is UNKNOWN, never affirmative availability.

rules.title: Cutoff immutability
rules.rule: Forecast/training cutoff objects and policy version are immutable lineage records.

rules.title: Training chronology
rules.rule: Historical training replay may use labels only from games completed/known before that model-training cutoff; each example feature row still uses its own pregame cutoff.
